doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Learning, living and the Colorado years
title: Learning visitors' music and the Caffe Lena approach
summary: Lamb gets players' charts ahead of time, at Louie's and now at Caffe Lena, and learns from their compositional ideas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Were these fellas, when they came in to sit in with your trio or be booked with your trio, did they bring charts? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

You know even back then, and I do that at my current gig at Caffe Lena, I want your music and I want to get your music before, you know like Louie’s was usually a couple of days before but I want to get your music so — I’m not a great sight reader, I’m working on it but I want to be able to know your music well enough when we’re presenting a concert for it to sound like that. Plus I learn, man, how much you learn doing that. You get into somebody else’s head, somebody else’s trip, somebody else’s compositional technique that to this day with the gig I’m doing, it’s like man —
Well you went to college after all.
